errors.english: except for that which is clean and has not been trodden upon
errors.why: The clause (continuing from the previous side's srog chags) excepts grass in which creatures do not breed; 'clean and not trodden upon' is not in the Tibetan.

errors.english: Udayin had them settle in a place
errors.why: gnas 'char ba is taking niśraya (formal dependence); Udāyin made the new monks take dependence on himself, not settle somewhere.

fix.find: Udayin had them settle in a place
fix.replace: Udayin had them take niśraya (dependence) on himself

errors.english: You will also be free from the burdens of carrying alms bowls, robes, nets, bowls, and belts, and free from the duties of receiving transmissions, reading, recitation, yoga, and mental cultivation.
errors.why: Udāyin promises the monks they will want for nothing in bowls, robes, etc. and in instruction, reading, recitation, yoga and attention (he will provide them); 'carrying' is added and the study duties are not presented as being dropped.

note: Readable narrative, but the key Vinaya term gnas 'char (taking niśraya) is lost and the opening exception is invented.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on cetanā and cetayitvā karma, with root verses correctly set off.

errors.english: Should not be despised in this world,
errors.why: The verse says the person should do what is not censured in this world and leads to happiness hereafter; the uncensured thing is the deed, not the person.

fix.find: Should not be despised in this world,
fix.replace: Should do what is not censured in this world,

errors.english: act like a spiritual teacher or a lord toward others
errors.why: The sentence (finished on the next side) says not to despise others, treating them as one's gurus or masters; the king is not told to act as a teacher or lord over them.

note: Good rendering of the Catuḥśataka commentary and its stories; one verse and the closing exhortation have their roles inverted.
Accurate presentation of the general/specific and literal/non-literal characteristics of the truths.

errors.english: found in the *Questions*
errors.why: gleng gzhi is Nidāna, the name of the Vinaya section quoted, not 'Questions'.

errors.english: the final part enters into the third portion
errors.why: gsum pa here is the third (instrumental) case: the grammatical rule is about the ending used in the instrumental, not a 'third portion'.

note: Karmavācanā technicalities (jñapti, jñaptidvitīya, jñapticaturtha) handled well; a source name and a grammatical term are misread.

errors.english: refers to one or two words unread.
errors.why: The gloss continues on the next side ('is a dwelling'); nothing in the Tibetan says words are unread.

fix.find: refers to one or two words unread.

errors.english: "It will be known by the unrest of you and the cowherd,"
errors.why: ma zhi ba is the cowherd's mother Śāntā (the same Śāntā whose hand throws the curd pot in the gloss), not 'unrest'.

fix.find: "It will be known by the unrest of you and the cowherd,"
fix.replace: "It will be known by you and Śāntā, the cowherd's mother,"

errors.english: the lake specifically named (Spilling-Vessel)
errors.why: spyi blugs is kamaṇḍalu, the ascetic's water-pot; the lake is named Kamaṇḍalu.

note: Most lexical glosses are fine, but a proper name is turned into 'unrest' and the final gloss is replaced by an invented 'words unread'.

errors.english: These are the summary verses:
errors.why: The phrase labels the preceding lines (rendered as prose) as summary verses; the English turns it into a heading for the following prose argument.

errors.english: regarding the entities dwelling in that subject
errors.why: gnas pa rnams are the disputants who take that subject as their basis and consider whether the object of the word 'pradhāna' has a real material cause, not entities residing in the subject.

note: Pramāṇa argument mostly followed, but the summary verses are rendered as prose and their label misplaced, garbling the structure.

errors.english: The engagement does not occur because of certainty.
errors.why: The reason, though it has the three modes, does not operate to produce certainty; certainty is the purpose that fails, not the cause of failure.

errors.english:
Is the sensation accompanied by the mosquito.
One knows with certainty: "This was created."
errors.why: One knows with certainty that 'this sensation was produced by something with a mosquito'; the English splits the content of the cognition across two clauses.

errors.english: the necessity that the effect cannot exist without the cause
errors.why: An unmarked explanatory gloss inserted into the verse; avinābhāva is not restricted to cause and effect.

errors.english: The three modes never exist separately.
errors.why: The verse says (the hetu's validity) never lies in the three modes; 'separately' is added and changes the claim.

note: Verse form preserved and most of Pātrasvāmin's anti-trairūpya argument is recognisable, but several lines are misconstrued.

errors.english: enters and rises from cessation, secluded from desires, secluded from unwholesome, non-virtuous states, accompanied by coarse investigation and subtle analysis, and possessing the joy and bliss born of seclusion, which is the first concentration.
errors.why: The Tathāgata enters the first dhyāna and rises from cessation (and the reverse in the next sentence); the English has him enter and rise from cessation.

fix.find: enters and rises from cessation, secluded from desires, secluded from unwholesome, non-virtuous states, accompanied by coarse investigation and subtle analysis, and possessing the joy and bliss born of seclusion, which is the first concentration.
fix.replace: enters the first concentration, which is secluded from desires, secluded from unwholesome, non-virtuous states, accompanied by coarse investigation and subtle analysis, and possessing the joy and bliss born of seclusion, and rises from cessation.

errors.english: the cause of transformation
errors.why: The phrase continues rnam par dag par from the previous side: the cause of [beings'] purification, not of 'transformation'.

note: Clean rendering of the sūtra quotation on causes of defilement and purification, except the dhyāna/cessation sequence is scrambled.

errors.english: does not include the limbs that are present here
errors.why: yan lag can is the whole (avayavin), not the limbs, and 'du ba is inherence (samavāya): variegatedness does not inhere in the whole in which it is present.

fix.find: does not include the limbs that are present here
fix.replace: does not inhere in the whole (avayavin) in which it is present here

errors.english: it is reasonable to call this inclusion "meeting in one object."
errors.why: 'du ba / don gcig la 'phrod pa 'du ba is (ekārtha)samavāya, inherence in one substrate, a Vaiśeṣika technical term, not 'inclusion' or 'meeting'.

errors.english: If a forest of a multitude of numbers
errors.why: The side opens by stating that the two cases are not alike; this sentence is not translated.

errors.english: the grasping of proximity has understanding of grasping simultaneously
errors.why: rig(s) pa dang ldan here means 'is reasonable': proximity-based apprehension is tenable for simultaneous apprehension, not for sequential.

note: The Vaiśeṣika vocabulary (samavāya, avayavin) is systematically misrendered, so the argument about citra cognition is hard to follow.
